title: Applications & Synthesis

competencies.text: Synthesize physics and chemistry principles in real-world applications.

days.title: Why Physics and Chemistry Work Together
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will synthesize physics and chemistry principles to explain real technologies and everyday processes.

🔗 Two Sciences, One System

Physics explains forces, motion, energy transfer, waves and electricity. Chemistry explains how substances react, bond and change. Most real systems need both: chemistry often stores or releases the energy, and physics describes how that energy moves and does work.

🔄 Follow the Energy

A good way to analyze any device is to trace the energy changes:

SystemEnergy chain
Jeepney enginechemical (diesel) → heat → kinetic (motion)
Phone batterychemical → electrical → light and sound
Solar panellight → electrical
Gas stove cooking ricechemical (LPG) → heat → chemical changes in food

At each arrow, ask: which part is chemistry (a reaction or change of substance)? and which part is physics (heat flow, motion, current, waves)? Energy is never created or destroyed — it only changes form, and some always becomes waste heat.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: In a jeepney engine, which step is mainly CHEMISTRY?

choices.label: Diesel burning with oxygen in the cylinder
Pistons pushing the crankshaft around
Gears turning the wheels at the back
Tires gripping the road surface using friction

scenario.explanation: Combustion is a chemical reaction that releases stored energy. Pistons, gears and tire friction are physics — forces and motion.

scenario.text: A phone battery powers the screen. What is the correct energy chain?

choices.label: Chemical → electrical → light
Light → chemical → electrical
Electrical → heat → chemical
Kinetic → chemical → electrical

scenario.explanation: Reactions inside the battery release energy as an electric current, and the screen turns that electrical energy into light.

scenario.text: Why does a running engine get hot even though its job is to make motion?

choices.label: Some energy always becomes waste heat
Engines create extra heat energy
Motion turns back into fuel inside
Heat is needed to keep the engine oil cold

scenario.explanation: No energy change is perfectly efficient. Part of the fuel's chemical energy always becomes heat instead of useful motion.

days.title: Case Studies: Batteries, Engines and Aircons
days.content:
🔋 Battery

Chemistry: a redox reaction — one electrode loses electrons (oxidation), the other gains them (reduction); ions move through the electrolyte.
Physics: the electrons flow through the outside wire as an electric current that powers the device. Charging pushes the reaction backward. A battery warms while charging because some electrical energy becomes heat.

🚙 Engine

Chemistry: fuel + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + heat (combustion).
Physics: hot gas pushes the piston; the crankshaft turns the push into rotation and torque; gears deliver it to the wheels.

❄️ Air Conditioner and Refrigerator

Chemistry: a refrigerant changes phase easily. It absorbs heat when it evaporates inside the room and releases heat when it condenses outside.
Physics: the compressor raises the gas's pressure and temperature; fans and coils transfer heat by convection and conduction. Heat is moved from inside to outside — the outdoor unit blows hot air.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each system or term to the physics + chemistry inside it. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Redox reaction drives an electric current
match.why: Chemistry releases electrons; physics describes their flow.

match.right: Combustion pushes pistons that turn a shaft
match.why: The reaction gives hot gas; the gas does mechanical work.

match.right: Absorbs heat as it evaporates indoors
match.why: Evaporation takes in heat, cooling the room.

match.right: Releases heat as the refrigerant condenses
match.why: That is why the outdoor unit blows hot air.
Light energy becomes electrical energy (photovoltaic effect).
Physical separation removes solids; chlorine kills germs.
Physics moves the heat; chemistry changes the food.
Solar heat drives evaporation; dissolved salt forms crystals.

days.title: Everyday Synthesis
days.content:
🍳 Cooking

Physics: heat moves from the flame to the pan by conduction, through boiling water by convection, and from charcoal to inihaw by radiation.
Chemistry: proteins denature (egg white turns solid), sugars caramelize, and the Maillard reaction browns bread and meat, creating flavor.

💧 Safe Drinking Water

A barangay system uses a pump (pressure and work), settling and filtration (separating solids by density and size) and chlorination (a chemical that kills microorganisms). Boiling at home uses heat to kill germs.

🧂 Salt Making in Pangasinan and Occidental Mindoro

Seawater is let into shallow beds. Solar energy evaporates the water (physics), and the dissolved sodium chloride crystallizes as the solution becomes saturated (chemistry).

🧠 Synthesis Strategy

  1. Name the goal of the system.
  2. List each step.
  3. Label each step physics or chemistry.
  4. Find where energy changes form and where it is wasted.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Explain real situations using both sciences. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A phone gets warm while charging. Which explanation uses BOTH sciences correctly?

choices.label: Current drives the reaction backward; some energy becomes heat
The battery burns oxygen and gives off smoke and heat
Light from the charger heats the battery's screen glass slowly
The phone's metal attracts heat from the charger wire

scenario.explanation: Charging is a reversed redox reaction (chemistry) driven by an electric current (physics). No conversion is perfect, so some energy becomes heat.

scenario.text: The outdoor unit of an aircon blows hot air. Why?

choices.label: The refrigerant releases room heat as it condenses
The compressor burns fuel to make cold air
Hot air is produced to balance the cold air
The fan heats up the outdoor air by spinning very fast

scenario.explanation: The refrigerant carried heat out of the room. Outside, it condenses and gives that heat off; the fan blows it away.

scenario.text: Bread turns brown and smells good when toasted. Which statement is MOST complete?

choices.label: Heat transfer starts the Maillard browning reaction
The bread absorbs light and changes its color
The toaster coats the bread with brown sugar
Water inside the bread turns brown when it is boiled

scenario.explanation: Physics (heat transfer from the coils) supplies the energy; chemistry (the Maillard reaction between sugars and proteins) makes the brown color and aroma.

scenario.text: A barangay's water is cloudy and sometimes causes diarrhea. Which plan BEST uses both sciences?

choices.label: Settle and filter the water, then add chlorine
Pump the water faster to make it cleaner
Add chlorine only and skip all the filtering
Store the water in a dark tank for a day

scenario.explanation: Settling and filtering (physics) remove particles, so the chlorine (chemistry) can reach and kill the remaining germs effectively.

scenario.text: A salt farmer's beds produce less salt during the rainy season. Which reason is BEST?

choices.label: Less sunlight and more rain slow the evaporation
Rain adds extra salt that dissolves the crystals
Cold weather makes the salt turn into sugar
Clouds pull the dissolved salt up into the air

scenario.explanation: Salt crystallizes only when water evaporates. Weak sunlight and added rainwater keep the solution from becoming saturated.

days.title: Designing with Both Sciences
days.content:
🛠️ From Explaining to Designing

Scientists and engineers use both sciences to solve problems. Example: "Keep vaccines cold in a far-flung barangay with frequent brownouts."

  • Physics ideas: insulation reduces heat conduction; a solar panel and battery keep power on; light-colored, shaded storage absorbs less radiation.
  • Chemistry ideas: ice packs and phase-change gels absorb heat as they melt; batteries store energy chemically.
  • Combined design: a solar-powered refrigerator with thick insulation and frozen gel packs as backup.

✅ Judging a Design

Ask: Does it follow the science (energy is conserved, reactions are safe)? Is it practical and affordable locally? What are the risks (fire, toxic chemicals, waste)? Can it be tested fairly?

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What kind of chemical reaction inside a battery produces electric current?

choices.label: Redox (oxidation–reduction)
Neutralization (acid–base)
Combustion (burning in air)
Precipitation (solid forming)

escape.explanation: One electrode loses electrons (oxidation) and the other gains them (reduction); the electrons flow through the circuit as current.

escape.text: Which step in a car engine changes chemical energy into heat?

choices.label: Combustion of fuel
Rotation of the gears
Friction of the tires
Turning of the steering

escape.explanation: Burning the fuel releases its stored chemical energy as heat and hot, expanding gas. The other steps are mechanical.

escape.text: An electric fan does NOT cool the air of a room. Which explanation combines both sciences?

choices.label: Moving air speeds up sweat evaporation, which takes heat from skin
The fan's motor removes heat from the air using a chemical reaction
The blades push hot air molecules out through the closed walls
The fan turns warm air into cold air by spinning very quickly

escape.explanation: Air movement (physics) speeds up evaporation, a change of state that absorbs heat from the skin. The air temperature itself does not drop.

escape.text: Which is the BEST example of physics and chemistry working together?

choices.label: A solar panel charging a battery
A ball rolling down a smooth ramp
A mirror reflecting a flashlight
A seesaw balancing two children

escape.explanation: The panel turns light into electricity (physics) and the battery stores it in a chemical reaction (chemistry). The others are physics only.

escape.text: To keep vaccines cold during brownouts, which design is MOST complete?

choices.label: Solar fridge plus insulation and frozen gel packs
A bigger electric fan blowing all day over the box
A metal box left in direct sunlight
A plastic bag filled with warm water

escape.explanation: Solar power keeps the fridge running, insulation slows heat flow, and gel packs absorb heat as they melt — physics and chemistry together.

escape.text: When seawater evaporates in a salt bed, what happens to the dissolved salt?

choices.label: It crystallizes as the water leaves
It evaporates along with the seawater
It turns into chlorine gas
It sinks back into the sea

escape.explanation: Salt does not evaporate at these temperatures. As water leaves, the solution becomes saturated and sodium chloride forms crystals.
